MPI-483 FIXED, doing/validating. Bug 1: /wrapper/disk ran `du -sb` and `-b` IS `--apparent-size`, so it summed declared LENGTHS - and the comment directly above the call asserted the opposite ('apparent-size off - real disk blocks, matches quota'), which is why two rewrites of that route (MPI-169, MPI-398) walked past it. Now `du -s --block-size=1` at BOTH call sites (/wrapper/disk and /wrapper/ls's per-top-level-dir breakdown). /wrapper/ls's file walk stays apparent on purpose - it is matched against declared dep sizes, not the quota - and that is now written at the call site. Wrapper source 0.2.43 -> 0.2.44 with a changelog entry in routes/remotePodLifecycle.js; the app's WRAPPER_VERSION pin stays 0.2.41 deliberately (an older wrapper answers the same shape, just inflated).

MPI-483 Bug 2: new pure exported volumeFitVerdict() in scripts/smoke-workflows.mjs, called right after the CPU download Pod comes up and BEFORE the first install - the earliest moment free space is knowable at all, since RunPod's API has only the configured size and the wrapper's du is the only live source. abort() deletes the live Pod on the way out, so a refusal costs minutes not a 40-minute fill. Units were the trap and are explicit: dep sizes are 1024-based GiB, RunPod volume sizes are base-10 GB. 7 asserts with a proven negative control in tests/smoke-free-space.test.cjs.

MPI-501 PROVEN LIVE 19:00Z. Fabio queued a generation on the LOCAL engine and hit the dev radial Restart Engine while it ran: the restart was REFUSED and ComfyUI kept running. That is navigation.js -> waitForIdleQueue against a real non-empty /queue - the leg the 04:15Z GPU run could not supply.

MPI-501 SURFACE FIXED in the same file. The refusal was emitted on `ui:error`, which shell.js:392 maps to showError() - the crash modal with an 'Error Summary (optional)' box and a REPORT ON GITHUB button. The guard working correctly was inviting a bug report against itself. Moved to `ui:warning` (statusBar.js:579 -> StatusBar.notify, 6s toast) and reworded: it had said 'then restart' to someone who had clicked Restart Engine a second earlier, and outside that dev-only radial (APP_CONFIG.dev_mode) nobody restarts ComfyUI by hand at all. The comfyController twin was CHECKED and deliberately left alone - comfy:error goes to the engine-start modal, not the GitHub dialog, and its wording never asks the user to restart.

npm test BACK TO GREEN, 530/530. It was red on master: 0b15f342 (MPI-505, H3 turbo) made stagesFor floor the TOTAL at 1 so H3 can pass a -1 delta for its single-pass run, which broke output-prompt-capture's pinned 'negative/garbage deltas must not corrupt a real count'. MPI-505 shipped without updating it and closed, so the break had no card. Re-pinned to 1 rather than adding a clamp: the sole caller (commandExecutor.js:1551, _enhanceBars + _singlePassBars) can only emit -1, 0 or +1, so a garbage delta is unreachable. A second assertion now pins the REAL case (-1 -> 1).

MPI-483's brief overstates its own bug 2: it says the preflight 'passed cleanly against a volume that could not fit the set'. The arithmetic disagrees - a 350 GB volume DOES hold the 322.7 GB set, so with honest numbers the gate passes and 2026-08-08 still proceeds. That day's false disk-full was bug 1 alone. Bug 2's fix stops a different class: a volume that genuinely cannot take the remainder.

NO CLAMP WAS ADDED TO stagesFor. The sole caller's delta domain is exactly {-1, 0, +1}, so a garbage delta cannot be produced and defending against it would be speculative. If someone adds a second caller with an unbounded delta, that decision changes.

I accused a sibling agent of VPN clock skew on the strength of a session-start GitHub anchor, then found ~10.5h of wall clock had passed across the gaps between turns while I kept deriving from it.
